page.layout: One page of text, single column, centred on the right-hand printed page; running head at top with page number; heading "Commentarius." centred below the verse-like italic passage; no margin notes on this page. A thin fragment of the facing (left) page is visible at the far right edge, which is show-through/edge and not transcribed.

p.i: Iam sunt; Habet tamen quod loquatur: Audiamus: Plebem decepi: Quid ad hoc forum? Philosophos non circumveni: Et cur insulsam istam ac turbulentam multitudinem elusisse, crimini sit? Repagulum ponimus, dum scite imponimus: Frœnum & flagellum sunt illi, quos suggerimus, instinctus: apprehendat hos prudens rector, utatur his: & domet, & agat quo vult, debili Rationi, vanis Legibus obluctantem semper & recalcitrantem feram.

main_text.head: Commentarius.
main_text.p: Equidem Actor ipse, quæ domige- rit Pantomimus, in bonam partem accipiebat (Tex. 13.) confabulantem cum Poëtis suis, ludentem cum ludionibus, dummodo sana, seria,

page.notes: The first line of the page carries the running head and the printed page number 56. The initial "E" of "Equidem" is a large woodcut-style initial, joined to the word. The sentence "Equidem ... seria," continues beyond the visible text; the lower part of the page is blank. Some words in the upper italic passage are slightly blurred but read with confidence.
